subject: Next steps: Dedicated capacity kickoff + sizing call

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@orchidpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Dedicated capacity kickoff + sizing call

Hi Samir —

Great talking earlier. Quick recap from our discovery: OrchidPay plans to route several high-throughput inference paths (fraud-check scoring, transaction summarization, and async embeddings) through a Dedicated GPU pool; targets are ~60k tokens/sec peak across batch windows with a P95 tail latency target of <200ms for the real-time scoring path. You flagged two priorities: (1) confirm throughput headroom for peak + burst (2) understand fallback routing to cheaper model variants.

Proposed immediate next step: a 60-minute Dedicated Capacity Sizing call (solutions deep dive) to align on real traffic shape and confirm the sizing and autoscale policy. Suggested attendees: Samir, your infra/ops lead (if available), Markus (solutions eng), Marissa (AE), and me.

Please pick one of these windows (PDT):
- Tue Apr 6, 10:00–11:00
- Wed Apr 7, 15:00–16:00
- Thu Apr 8, 08:30–09:30

Pre-reads I can send before the call:
- capacity-checklist.xlsx (short checklist to capture load shape + SLOs)
- example traffic sample for parsing (I can accept CSV/JSON)

If those times don't work, tell me two options that do and we'll lock it. I'll send a calendar invite once we confirm.

Best,
Neha Kapoor | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Thanks Neha — appreciate the clear recap. Wed Apr 7 15:00 PDT works best for me and I'll loop in Rajiv (our infra lead) — copying him now.

Quick notes before the call:
- We can pull a 48-hour production trace for the scoring path; will that be useful?
- For fallback, we currently have an in-house cheaper model; curious what the ops impact is for automatic fallback.

I'll accept whichever invite you send. Could you also send the capacity checklist so Rajiv can prep?

Cheers,
Samir

Perfect — Wed Apr 7 at 15:00 PDT is locked.

Actions before the call:
1) Samir / Rajiv: please share a 48-hour trace (JSON or CSV) for the scoring path and an example request/response shape. If you're short on time, a sample of 1k requests representative of peak is fine.
2) Rajiv: any SLO docs you already have (p95/p99 targets) will help us map queueing + batch sizes.
3) Markus / me: we'll prepare a draft autoscale policy (+ recommended buffer headroom) and a fallback plan for model variants.

I've attached the capacity checklist and an example traffic sample schema to this thread. If you prefer, I can create a short Google Drive folder and drop the items there — let me know.

See you Wednesday. I'll send the calendar invite in a sec.

Best,
Neha
